page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.xlarge is a local storage and memory-oriented cloud server built on the KVM hypervisor platform. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the system exposes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. Hardware resources include 32 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, and a dedicated 959 GB local SSD storage volume. Network connectivity is capped at a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Benchmark assessments locate the compute and memory throughput performance of the ecs.i2ne.xlarge within the lower quartile relative to standard server benchmarks. Single-threaded and multi-threaded CPU execution via stress-ng registered 1101.89 and 2923.84 points respectively, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations scored 941.0 and 2049.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 20.18 GB/sec alongside write speeds of 18.64 GB/sec. Synthetic database benchmarks yielded 1081.7 operations per second on PassMark tests, static web serving throughput reached 2.52 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations logged 2.97 million requests per second.

With 8 GB of memory allocated per vCPU alongside an integrated local SSD, the instance prioritizes memory density and local disk access over raw compute capacity. The hardware tradeoff trades high single-thread processor efficiency for higher RAM capacity per vCPU and local storage availability. The overall resource combination fits memory-intensive utility tasks, local database caching layers, staging environment databases, log indexing engines, and general data buffering where maximum processing speeds are not mandatory.
